seo.title: Aluminum Weight Calculator - Sheet & Plate
seo.description: Aluminum Weight Calculator — Calculate the weight of aluminum parts including sheets, plates, and extrusions with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Weight = L × W × T × ρ. Aluminum density = 2700 kg/m³ (about 1/3 the weight of steel).

content.introduction: Calculate the weight of aluminum sheets, plates, and flat parts. Aluminum density is 2700 kg/m³ — roughly one-third of steel, making it ideal for lightweight structures.

faq.a: Pure aluminum is 2700 kg/m³. Aluminum alloys range from 2640 to 2850 kg/m³ depending on alloying elements.

faq.q: How much lighter is aluminum than steel?
faq.a: Aluminum is about 65% lighter than carbon steel for the same volume (2700 vs 7850 kg/m³).

faq.q: How do I calculate the weight of an aluminum sheet?
faq.a: Multiply length x width x thickness (in meters) by density (2700 kg/m3). Example: 1000 x 500 x 5 mm sheet = 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.005 x 2700 = 6.75 kg.

faq.q: What is the density of 6061 aluminum?
faq.a: 6061 aluminum has a density of 2700 kg/m3 (2.70 g/cm3). It is the most common structural alloy, used for extrusions, plates, and machined parts.

faq.q: How much does an aluminum plate weigh?
faq.a: A 2000 x 1000 x 10 mm 6061 plate weighs 54 kg. The same carbon steel plate weighs 157 kg — aluminum is about 2.9x lighter for the same dimensions.

faq.q: How do I convert mm to meters in the formula?
faq.a: Divide each mm dimension by 1000. Example: 1000 mm = 1.0 m, 500 mm = 0.5 m, 5 mm = 0.005 m. Then multiply the three dimensions by density (2700 kg/m3) to get weight in kg.

sections.heading: Aluminum Weight Formula Explained
sections.body:
Weight is volume times density:

W = L x W x T x rho

Where L, W, T = length, width, thickness (m), rho = density (kg/m3). Convert mm inputs to meters first (divide by 1000).

Example: a 1000 x 500 x 5 mm aluminum sheet: V = 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.005 = 0.0025 m3, W = 0.0025 x 2700 = 6.75 kg. The same sheet in steel (7850 kg/m3) weighs 19.6 kg — aluminum is about 2.9x lighter for the same volume.

sections.heading: Common Aluminum Alloy Densities
sections.body:
| Alloy | Density (kg/m3) | Typical Use |
|---|---|---|
| 1050 (pure) | 2705 | Electrical, food |
| 3003 | 2730 | Sheet, cookware |
| 5052 | 2680 | Marine, tanks |
| 6061 | 2700 | Structural, extrusions |
| 6063 | 2700 | Architectural extrusions |
| 7075 | 2810 | Aerospace, high strength |

Most structural alloys fall in the 2680-2810 kg/m3 range. Using 2700 kg/m3 is accurate to within 2% for common grades like 6061 and 6063.

sections.heading: Worked Example: Sheet and Plate Weight
sections.body:
A 2000 x 1000 x 10 mm 6061 aluminum plate:

V = 2.0 x 1.0 x 0.01 = 0.02 m3
W = 0.02 x 2700 = 54 kg

Compare: the same carbon steel plate weighs 157 kg (7850 kg/m3) — aluminum saves 103 kg, about 66%. For a 6 m x 1 m x 3 mm sheet: V = 0.018 m3, W = 48.6 kg. Use the calculator for any flat part; for round bar or pipe use the dedicated weight calculators.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Aluminum Weight
sections.body:
**Weight units**

- 1 kg = 2.20462 lb
- 1 tonne = 1000 kg
- 1 lb = 0.4536 kg

**Length units**

- 1 m = 3.28084 ft
- 1 inch = 25.4 mm

**Density units**

- 1 kg/m³ = 0.06243 lb/ft³

Aluminum density is about 2700 kg/m³ (6061: 2700, 7075: 2810). Weight = density × volume. Convert all dimensions to one consistent unit system before computing, then convert the result to the required weight unit.
